text: A con man played a Saudi prince for about thirty years. One dinner order ended it.
He tells Miami investors he's royalty. So— okay, how do you check that?
Then there's the Ferrari with diplomatic plates, and bodyguards with diplomatic security badges.
Tap the heart if you'd believe him.
Investors did, and it cost them more than eight million dollars.
But the plates and badges were fake.
Send this to the friend who thinks nice cars mean money.
It gets dumber. Prosecutors said he'd been arrested or convicted eleven times for this.
He was sentenced to more than eighteen years in prison. So what cracked it?
Follow, this page never skips the tell.
Then, at dinner, the prince ordered pork. The royal he was playing wouldn't eat it.
A victim noticed. Which would you catch: plates, or the dinner order?
